name: presence
description: Content arriving and leaving (ADR 0028). A wrapper with no element of its own: each keyed child is an item that Presence animates in on --ui-duration-base through CSS @starting-style and out on --ui-duration-fast, keeping a removed child rendered — inert, aria-hidden — until its exit's transitions finish, and moving focus inside it to a neighbour first. Three kinds: fade, rise (a lift of --ui-space-xs × --ui-motion-travel) and collapse (the item's measured height opens and folds, fading first, so the rows below glide). Items present at mount do not animate unless appear is set. All CSS transitions on the motion tokens, so the motion levels need no code and a re-added item turns around mid-exit.

/** * Typed documentation for Presence. * * One source for the docs site, Storybook autodocs and MCP answers. Prose that * is not here does not exist as far as tooling is concerned (CONVENTIONS §11). */ export const presenceDoc = { lead: "Animates content as it arrives and leaves, and keeps leaving content on screen until it has gone.", name: "Presence", status: "experimental", summary: "The first of ADR 0028's owned motion components. A wrapper with no element and no look of its own: each keyed child is an item, and Presence gives every arrival and exit in an app the same timing. Three kinds — fade (the default), rise (fade plus a lift of --ui-space-xs, for content landing in a stream), collapse (the whole box opens and folds — height, vertical padding, border and margin — for rows in a list, so nothing below jumps). Arrivals run on --ui-duration-base with --ui-ease-out through CSS @starting-style; exits fade on --ui-duration-fast and never travel; collapse fades and folds together, so the list closes over the row in one motion. A removed child stays rendered — inert, aria-hidden, its last content — until its exit's transitions finish, and focus inside it moves to a neighbour first. Items present on the first render do not animate unless `appear` is set. Everything is a CSS transition on the motion tokens, so the motion levels need no code here, and a child added back mid-exit turns around from the frame it is on. Base UI surfaces (Popover, Modal, Sheet, Toast…) already own their presence and are not wrapped.", anatomy: [ { part: "presence", slot: "none", notes: "The root renders no element, so it can sit inside a list, a stack or a toolbar without changing the layout — and a Presence of
  • stays valid HTML inside a
      . It owns the list of items, including the departing ones it still renders.", }, { part: "item", slot: "the caller's", notes: "Each child element. Presence writes data-presence (entering · present · leaving), its transition classes (merged after the child's own className) and a ref onto it, so the child must forward className, ref and data-* to its DOM node — every component in this library does (CONVENTIONS §5). While leaving it is inert and aria-hidden. For collapse its height is set inline from a measurement while it moves, with overflow clipped, and cleared once it settles.", }, ], composition: ` Presence (kind?, appear?) └── item — any element with a stable key, forwarding className/ref/data-* ├── data-presence="entering" — arrived after mount; plays the entrance once ├── data-presence="present" └── data-presence="leaving" — the caller removed it; inert until its exit ends
        {tasks.map((task) =>
      • {task.title}
        • )}
      `, props: { kind: { type: '"fade" | "rise" | "collapse"', default: '"fade"', notes: "fade for anything in place. rise for content landing in a stream — a new message, a toast's row — where the lift says where it came from; the lift is --ui-space-xs × --ui-motion-travel, so at Reduced it is a plain fade. collapse for rows in a list, where the space itself has to open and close. Timing is not a prop: every Presence in an app arrives and leaves the same way, which is the point of having one.", }, appear: { type: "boolean", default: "false", notes: "Play the entrance for the items present on the first render too. Off by default, because a page that loads a list should show the list rather than perform it. On for the case where one action both mounts the Presence and adds the row — opening a panel that shows the item just created.", }, children: { type: "ReactNode", notes: "Keyed elements. The key is how Presence tells a removal from a change: a list re-keyed by index animates the wrong rows. Children without a key are keyed by position, and text children are not rendered.", }, }, do: [ "Give every item a stable key from the data, never the array index.", "Show the change first, then remove the row: update its label or tick, wait for it to land, then drop it from the list.", "Keep what arrived readable without the motion: the new row's text, a count, a status line in a live region you own.", "Use collapse inside lists, so the rows below glide instead of jumping.", ], dont: [ "Wrap a Popover, Modal, Sheet, Drawer, Select, Menu or Toast. They mount and unmount through the behaviour layer with their own motion, and would animate twice.", "Put your own transition on the item. Presence owns `transition` on it, and two transition declarations on one element do not combine — one silently wins.", "Pass a component that does not forward className and ref to its DOM node. Nothing will animate, and the leaving item will stay until its (absent) exit ends — immediately.", "Use it to announce anything. Presence is silent; announcements belong in a live region the caller owns.", ], a11y: { role: "None. Presence adds no element and no semantics; each item keeps the role it already has.", name: "None.", keyboard: [], focus: "A leaving item is made inert only after focus inside it has moved to the nearest item that is not leaving — the next one, or the previous one at the end of the list — so the reader's place is never dropped to . If no neighbour has anything focusable, focus is released.", contrastPairs: [], rendersNoColour: "Presence renders no element and sets no colour: it changes only opacity, translate and height on the caller's own items, whose pairs are the caller's component's to declare.", }, forwarding: { className: "Not accepted on Presence itself: there is no element to put it on. Each item's own className is kept and Presence's classes merge after it.", ref: "Not accepted on Presence. An item's own ref is preserved and merged with the one Presence attaches.", props: "Presence takes only kind, appear and children. Everything else belongs on the items.", }, motion: "Everything is a CSS transition on the tokens, never a keyframe, so a reversed change turns around mid-flight. Arrival: --ui-duration-base, --ui-ease-out, from @starting-style (opacity 0; rise also translate --ui-space-xs × --ui-motion-travel; collapse also its box closed — height, vertical padding, border and margin, measured at rest and set inline — with the fade half a fast step behind the fold, so the room opens before the content shows). Exit: opacity on --ui-duration-fast, nothing travels; collapse folds its whole box on --ui-duration-base at the same moment, never after the fade. Height alone cannot fold a padded row: with border-box sizing it stops at padding + border. Motion levels (ADR 0028): at Reduced rise becomes a plain fade (travel 0) and collapse still eases, being change in place, capped at --ui-duration-base; at Off every duration is 1ms, and a leaving item is still removed only once that 1ms transition has finished, never synchronously. Removal waits for the item's OWN transitions, never its subtree, where a spinner never finishes.", needsDesign: [], knownGaps: [ "The Presence sheet drew collapse's height as a wrapper animating grid-template-rows. Built instead as the item's own height, measured and set inline: a wrapper element inside a
        is invalid HTML, and Presence promises no element of its own. The sheet's Fold row records the change.", "Focus moves only within one Presence. A list whose last item leaves hands focus to nothing; the caller should move it to the list's heading or its add control.", "Count, TextSwap, IconSwap, Stagger and Feedback — the other five owned motion components in ADR 0028 — are not built yet.", ], design: "https://app.paper.design/file/01KZ39A2BC286MT85M658NRR4R/8-0/489K-1", } as const;
